Top Tourist Attractions in China

From the Great Wall to the Forbidden City – your comprehensive guide to the greatest historical and cultural landmarks

🏛️ 10 Main Attractions⏱️ 10 min read📅 Updated 2026
Home◂Tourism in China◂Tourist Attractions

China has more than 56 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, making it one of the world's richest countries in archaeological and historical landmarks. From great walls to imperial palaces, from Buddhist temples to stunning archaeological discoveries – China offers a journey through thousands of years of civilization, art and architecture. Arcadia Tourism facilitates visits to these landmarks within comprehensive travel programs with Arabic-speaking guides.

1. The Great Wall of China 🧱

The Great Wall of China is China's most famous attraction and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. The wall stretches over 21,000 kilometers across mountains and valleys, built over many centuries to protect the empire from invasions. The best sections to visit are Mutianyu (least crowded with the most beautiful views), Badaling (easiest access) and Jinshanling (for adventurers). Walking on the wall is an unforgettable experience – read more about it in Tourist Activities.

2. The Forbidden City (Imperial Palace) 🏛️

The Forbidden City in the heart of Beijing is the world's largest palace complex, built in the 15th century and the residence of 24 emperors from the Ming and Qing dynasties. It contains more than 9,000 rooms across 72 hectares, featuring stunning imperial Chinese architecture with its golden roofs and red walls. The complex is now a museum housing priceless royal collections.

3. The Terracotta Army ⚔️

The Terracotta Army in Xi'an is one of the greatest archaeological discoveries in history. Discovered by chance in 1974, it contains more than 8,000 life-size statues of soldiers, horses and war chariots, created to guard the tomb of Emperor Qin Shi Huang. Each statue is unique with different facial features and expressions, making it an unparalleled work of art.

4. Temple of Heaven 🌏

The Temple of Heaven in Beijing is an imperial religious complex built in 1420. Emperors visited it to pray for abundant harvests. It is distinguished by its unique circular geometric design and decorated blue dome without central support columns – a stunning architectural achievement. It is surrounded by a large park used by locals for tai chi in the mornings.

5. The Summer Palace 🏞️

The Summer Palace in Beijing is the largest preserved imperial garden in China. It spans more than 290 hectares, three-quarters of which is covered by Kunming Lake. Built in the 18th century as a summer retreat for the imperial family, it features the Long Corridor decorated with more than 14,000 paintings and the Buddhist Temple overlooking the lake.

6. Longmen Grottoes 🗿

The Longmen Grottoes near Luoyang contain more than 100,000 Buddhist statues carved into rock over four centuries. The largest is the Vairocana Buddha statue at 17 meters tall. They are considered one of the finest examples of Buddhist art in East Asia and are listed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

7. Great Mosque of Xi'an 🕌

The Great Mosque of Xi'an is one of the oldest and largest mosques in China, dating back to 742 AD. It features unique architecture that blends traditional Chinese style with Islamic art. Located in the heart of the historic Muslim Quarter, it remains an active mosque to this day. Read more about mosques and halal food in China Halal Guide.

8. Oriental Pearl Tower 🗼

The Oriental Pearl Tower in Shanghai is one of China's most famous modern landmarks. It rises 468 meters and features a unique design with multiple spherical balls. It contains panoramic observation decks with transparent glass floors, and the Shanghai History Museum on the lower floor.

💡 Arcadia Tip

To visit China's major attractions you need a program of at least 10–14 days. We recommend starting from Beijing (3–4 days) then Xi'an (2–3 days) then Shanghai (2–3 days). Check out the ready-made travel programs or contact us to design a custom program. Also check cost of tourism in China to plan your budget.
